description: "Use when: writing user-facing copy, documentation tone, terminology for Deaf users, or emoji usage"

# Language

## General

- Keep language simple, warm and clear.
- Use short sentences and plain language that someone without a software background can understand.
- Avoid jargon.
- Use emojis to add expression, not as decoration.

## Wordings

### Technical terms

In ordinary prose, lowercase generic technical terms such as "origin header". Preserve standard capitalization for exact protocol identifiers, such as the HTTP field name `Origin` or the literal `Origin:`.

### Users

Videomail serves Deaf users and people who want to learn sign language. Use inclusive, respectful language. Do not use "hearing impaired" or "deaf-mute"; use "Deaf" or "hard of hearing".

Sign language is visual, so emojis can help make copy expressive. Use them with care.

### Developers

Make developer-facing responses enjoyable to read. A little humor is welcome, but keep it useful.
